The explicit panic rule overrides a naive reading of general interface comparability for a shared incomparable dynamic type. Static interface comparability permits forming a comparison but does not guarantee that evaluation succeeds. Both operands are interface values with identical dynamic types, and that dynamic type is not comparable. Different dynamic types or a nil interface operand do not satisfy this condition. This does not make arbitrary equality expressions statically legal. A slice held in both operands' dynamic values fits the trigger, while a slice in only one operand or an interface compared with nil does not.
